sec: Adrenomedullin, pheochromocytoma definition and the types tree · p853

items.exp: Adrenomedullin is produced from endothelium; it causes vasodilation and inhibits endothelial cell apoptosis (prevents septic shock). (Book p853)

items.q: The other granule contents of the medulla listed are:
items.exp: Other contents of granules: opioids and chromogranin A. (Book p853)

items.q: Pheochromocytoma typically presents in which decades, with what sex ratio?
Pheochromocytoma is defined as a neural-crest cell tumour producing:
items.exp: Definition: neural crest cell tumour producing catecholamines (pulsatile) and catecholamine metabolites. (Book p853)

items.q: By origin, adrenal pheochromocytoma and extra-adrenal paraganglioma split as:
items.exp: Adrenal 75%; extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma 25% with high malignant potential. (Book p853)

items.q: The m/c site of sympathetic-ganglia paraganglioma (20%) is the:
items.exp: Sympathetic ganglia (20%): m/c site organ of Zuckerkandl. (Book p853)

items.q: Parasympathetic paragangliomas (5%) are typically non-functional; their m/c site is:
items.exp: Parasympathetic ganglia (5%): non-functional; m/c site carotid body > jugular bulb. (Book p853)

items.q: ‘Page 852 says extra-adrenal tumours secrete only NE (no PNMT), yet the p853 types tree prints ‘produce only NA’ under the adrenal branch and ‘adrenaline > NA’ under extra-adrenal — the PNMT mechanism (p852) is the one to apply in answers.’
opts: True — the tree print conflicts with the PNMT mechanism
False — p852 says adrenal lacks PNMT
items.exp: The book's own p852 mechanism (PNMT adrenal-only, extra-adrenal = NE only) conflicts with the printed p853 tree labels; learn the mechanism. (Book p853)

items.q: The CURRENT statistics that replaced the obsolete ‘rule of 10’ are:
items.exp: Obsolete rule of 10 = 10% each; current: bilateral 40%, extra-adrenal 25%, familial 40%, malignant 50%. (Book p853)

items.q: Familial pheochromocytoma (40% currently) is associated with, and the STRONGEST association is:
items.exp: Familial cases occur in young patients; associated with MEN (strongest association), VHL (von Hippel-Lindau), NF-1 (neurofibromatosis). (Book p853)

items.q: Familial pheochromocytomas are usually bilateral EXCEPT when associated with:
items.exp: Usually B/L except NF-1 associated (U/L). (Book p853)

items.q: The surest sign of malignant pheochromocytoma and the mutation raising metastatic potential are:
items.exp: Surest sign = metastasis; SDH-B ↑ metastatic potential. (Book p853)
